$\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln\left(\dfrac{1-3x}{1+2x}\right)=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\ln(1-3x)-\ln(1+2x)\right]$

Stationary points: $f'(x)=0$, so $x=-2$ or $x=1$; $f(-2)=0$, $f(1)=27$. Points $(-2,0)$ and $(1,27)$.

$f''(1)=-12(1)(3)=-36<0$, so $(1,27)$ is a maximum turning point.

$f''(-2)=0$ and $f'(-2)=0$; test concavity: $f''(-3)=-36$ (concave down), $f''(-1)=12$ (concave up). The concavity changes, so $(-2,0)$ is a horizontal point of inflection.

Tangent at $B$: $y-3=\dfrac3e\left(x-(e-2)\right)$, so $ey-3e=3x-3e+6$, giving $3x-ey+6=0$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: some correct progress to the gradient of the tangent to $g(x)$; 1: gradient at $B$ equals $\frac3e$; 1: correct equation in general form (1/2 deducted if fractions in general form)

$A_{\triangle OPM}=\tfrac12\times OP\times OM\times\sin\theta=\tfrac12\times5\times2\times\sin\theta=5\sin\theta$.

$A_{\triangle ONP}=\tfrac12\times ON\times OP\times\sin\left(\tfrac\pi2-\theta\right)=\tfrac12\times4\times5\times\cos\theta=10\cos\theta$.

So $A_{OMPN}=A_{\triangle OPM}+A_{\triangle ONP}=5\sin\theta+10\cos\theta$, as required.

solutions.latex:
$A=5\sin\theta+10\cos\theta$, so $\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=5\cos\theta-10\sin\theta$.

For maximum area $\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=0$: $10\sin\theta=5\cos\theta$, $\tan\theta=\dfrac12$, $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac12\right)=0.463\ldots$ radians.

$\dfrac{d^2A}{d\theta^2}=-5\sin\theta-10\cos\theta\approx-11.18<0$, so this is a maximum turning point. Maximum area occurs when $\tan\theta=\dfrac12$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: differentiating correctly; 1: solving for $\tan\theta=\frac12$; 1: testing the stationary point and showing it is a maximum (1/2 deducted if $\theta$ in degrees)

solutions.latex:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac12=\dfrac yx$, so $y=\dfrac x2$. Also $x^2+y^2=25$.

Substituting: $x^2+\dfrac{x^2}{4}=25$, $5x^2=100$, $x^2=20$, $x=2\sqrt5$, and then $y=\sqrt5$.

$P=(2\sqrt5,\sqrt5)$.

Alternative: $\sin\theta=\dfrac1{\sqrt5}$, $\cos\theta=\dfrac2{\sqrt5}$, so $y=5\sin\theta=\sqrt5$ and $x=5\cos\theta=2\sqrt5$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: some correct progress; 1: correct final answer (1/2 deducted if not in surd form)
